subject: Capacity snapshot + burst storyboard — post-demo follow-up
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena@shipmate.io>, qa_ops@shipmate.io
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.inference>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Capacity snapshot + burst storyboard — post-demo follow-up

Elena / ShipMate team — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we don't lose momentum.

Key notes from call:
- Latency target: 95th percentile under 400ms for interactive checkout flows (single-turn text completion, ~300 token responses).
- Throughput shape: baseline steady-state ~45 QPS for authentication/lookup traffic; expected burst crest to ~420 QPS for 90–120s windows during event-driven promotions.
- Streaming: 60% of sessions will use streaming responses (progressive recommendations). Streaming sessions maintain longer open connections (~6–12s) and are sensitive to per-token latency.
- Concurrency: concurrency of long-running sessions estimated at 220 simultaneous streaming connections at peak.
- Token velocity: average response ~280 tokens; peak tokens/sec during crest ~118K tokens/sec.

What I'm attaching: a lightweight capacity snapshot and a visual "burst storyboard" that maps event triggers to expected QPS/token bursts. Open for edits.

Suggested next steps (please pick items you want us to drive):
1) You: confirm whether promo crest is 90s or 120s.
2) Your infra/QA: share a short list of representative request traces (anonymized) or a sampling from the last 30-day peak window.
3) Redwood: run a preliminary capacity estimate and propose a minimal Dedicated profile that meets 95th/400ms and handles the crest with graceful degrade.
4) All: sync next Wednesday to validate estimate and discuss canary strategy.

If you want me to prioritize the steady-state optimization (smaller Dedicated + aggressive caching) vs. burst-ready configuration (larger headroom + fallback models), call that out and we'll model both.

Thanks — Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0172

Attachments: capacity_snapshot_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), burst_storyboard_v2.png (image)

From: Elena Ortiz <elena@shipmate.io>

Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 18:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Capacity snapshot + burst storyboard — post-demo follow-up

Thanks Karthik — this is helpful. A couple clarifications from our side:

- Crest duration: typically 100–110s; the 120s number was an upper-bound. Use 110s for modeling.
- Streaming split: the 60% is an estimate; QA will validate with traces and revert.
- Token calculation: our responses vary; we have some locale-based expansions that push average up to ~340 tokens in EN-US peak flows. You should model both 280 and 340 tokens.

Action items for us: we'll pull a 48-hour sample (anonymized) and drop it in the SFTP by EOD tomorrow. QA will also flag any flows that must be low-latency (cart finalization, auth).

Elena
Director, Platform Engineering
ShipMate

>

> 
> Karthik

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.inference>

Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:33:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Capacity snapshot + burst storyboard — post-demo follow-up

Elena / ShipMate QA — hi, Grace from Solutions Engineering. A few implementation notes from our side that will shape the capacity model: 

- For streaming sessions, we recommend keeping the per-token processing path quantized to int8 for the 95th latency target; that reduces per-token compute by ~22% in our tests. We'll include a comparison in the table.
- Based on your crest/token numbers, the recommended approach is a hybrid: modest Dedicated baseline sized to handle 1.2x steady-state plus an autoscaling headroom layer for the crest. We'll show a fallback policy to a lower-cost model variant (smaller memory footprint) when latency SLO is non-critical for some sub-flows.
- For concurrency: if your load balancer upper-bound exceeds 1,000 simultaneous TLS sessions, we can recommend a connection proxy pattern to offload keep-alives and reduce GPU slot pressure.

I'll attach a short checklist in the next message and a first-pass cost delta for steady vs burst.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena@shipmate.io>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 22 Apr 2027 10:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Capacity snapshot + burst storyboard — post-demo follow-up

Elena — quick cost snapshot attached below. We modelled two scenarios using your 110s crest and the 340-token peak:

Scenario A — Steady-lean (optimize cost):
- Dedicated baseline: 6 x L4 GPUs (quantized int8)
- Autoscale headroom: warm pool of 2 L4s for short bursts, spill to preemptible for 5–10% overflow
- Estimated incremental cost vs hosted: +18% for guaranteed 95th <400ms

Scenario B — Burst-resilient (optimize availability):
- Dedicated baseline: 10 x L4 GPUs (mixed precision for low-latency paths)
- Autoscale headroom: 6 additional GPUs (burst window coverage)
- Fallback: lighter model variant for non-critical flows
- Estimated incremental cost vs hosted: +52% for consistent crest handling with <400ms 95th

Immediate asks for us to finalize numbers:
1) 48-hour trace upload (SFTP path) — controls the token histogram and session hold times.
2) Confirmation if certain flows can accept 800ms 95th during crest (this materially lowers cost).
3) Your preferred date/time for the calibration call (we suggested Wed in the original note; propose Wed 28 Apr at 1700 UTC).

If acceptable, we'll convert Scenario A into a recommended Dedicated sizing + rollout checklist and provide a canary plan for live traffic cutover with rollback triggers.

Thanks — Monica
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.inference
